sections.hypothesis: Buying liquid coins in an uptrend after an oversold close below the 2.5 SD Bollinger band and a further intraday drop (a limit 3% under that close), and selling at the first bounce, beats the large-basket control and BTC at the same exposure on Sharpe, after costs.
sections.rationale: Who pays: short-term liquidity provision. Impatient or forced sellers push a coin below its recent range; a resting bid that buys a further drop is paid a premium when the price recovers (short-term reversal: Jegadeesh 1990, Lehmann 1990; in equities Connors' and Rayner Teo's pullback systems). Requiring the coin to be above its 200-day keeps it to dips in coins that are trending up, not falling knives. Outside evidence: Rayner Teo's Russell 1000 backtest 2000-2025 (+2,834%, 66% winners, payoff under 1, drawdown 27%; Luke's YouTube batch 3 G1), and batch 2's validation study, where mean reversion was the only family positive on average out of sample. Against it, honestly: it is the dip family. Kestrel's buy-big-down-days, Fear & Greed contrarian and extreme-fear tests failed on BTC and ETH, and the entry bar names reversals as rejected. Across many alts, with a trend filter and a limit entry, it is untested here. Kestrel's universe keeps delisted coins, so the survivorship bias the spec warns about in Rayner's test can't flatter this one. Freezing this note is Luke's knowing override of the entry bar.
sections.rules: bollinger-pullback, daily bars, the coin universe (delisted coins included). Eligible coins: 180 days of unbroken history and a 30-day median quote volume of at least 20M USDT. Setup at a close: above its 200-day average and below the 20-day Bollinger band at 2.5 SD. Then a limit buy at 3% under that close for the next day only, filled at the lower of the limit and the open if the low reaches it (kestrel.backtest.portfolio limit entries; costs as a market order, which is conservative). With more setups than free slots, the highest 150-day return first. At most 3 coins at a third each; held coins are kept as they are, not trimmed. Sell at the next open after a close with RSI(2) above 50, or after the 10th close since the fill. No price stop, as in the original. 330 USDT, costs from kestrel.toml with each coin's spread band. Period 2020-01 to 2025-10, before the holdout.
sections.falsification: Against the large-basket control and BTC at the same exposure, with the full scorecard. Fails on any failed test. The spec's extra check: the win rate must stay high enough to be positive with a payoff under 1. Random entry (test 9) doesn't apply: it is built for one-coin bracket strategies, and this one holds a basket of weights.
sections.parameters: band_sd_tenths 25 (2.5 SD), depth_pct 3, max_days 10, top_n 3, trend_days 200, btc_filter 0, min_history_days 180, min_volume_musd 20. Three runs: Rayner's rule (2.5 SD, 3%), a deeper limit for crypto's volatility (2.5 SD, 7%), and the BTC filter variant (2.5 SD, 3%, btc_filter 1). The spec's full 3 x 3 sweep of band and depth is not run (it would be 9 trials); the robustness check moves each parameter around the first setting (about 25 neighbours).
sections.costs: A trade lasts 1-10 days. Setups are frequent across a basket: perhaps 50-150 round trips a year, at 22-40 bps each: 1.5-5% a year in costs, against average wins of a few percent. Trials: 3 runs plus about 25 neighbours.
